data.purge_days: Remove after days without a sighting

data_description.host: Address of the UniFi controller, without https://

error.cannot_connect: Connection failed. Check host and API key.

polling.name: Polling
polling.description: How often the integration queries the controller.

data_description.scan_interval: How often the client list is fetched from the controller.

cleanup.name: Automatic removal
cleanup.description: When clients the controller no longer reports disappear from Home Assistant.

data.purge_days: Remove after days without a sighting

data_description.purge_days: Client and device are removed after this many days without a sighting. 0 disables removal.
data_description.purge_time:
Time of the daily cleanup run, local time. The integration checks how long each client has not been seen. Anything past the threshold loses its entities and its device in Home Assistant; the report is then sent as a notification.

If “Remove after days without a sighting” is set to 0, nothing runs and this time has no effect.

A check also runs 60 seconds after each Home Assistant start. It only reports when something was actually removed, so a restart does not produce a message.

Independently of this you can trigger the run at any time via the unifi_dynamic.purge_now action, optionally as a dry run.
data_description.purge_exclude: Selected clients are never removed automatically, no matter how long they have not been seen. The list contains every client the integration knows, with name and MAC. Leave empty to apply the threshold above to all.

push.name: Push notification
push.description: Target, triggers and content of the messages to your phone. The «Content» checkboxes decide which details appear in the message about newly detected devices. If all of them are off, the display name is reported instead.

data.notify_when_empty: Also report when nothing was removed

data_description.notify_service: notify service or notify entity, for example a notify group.
data_description.notify_when_empty: Enabled means a push after every daily run, even with no hits. Off by default.
data_description.notify_new_clients: Push notification as soon as a client appears in the UniFi API for the first time. The “Content” checkboxes decide which details it contains. If one of them is not available yet, for example because the DHCP lease is not through, the message waits for up to 120 seconds and is sent as soon as everything is there. SSID and access point are only waited for on wireless clients. After that the message is sent with whatever is available. Nothing is reported during the initial fill after installation, otherwise every existing client would trigger a message. If more than five clients appear at once, a single summary is sent instead. Does not create a persistent notification.
data_description.message_name: Name from the controller, otherwise DHCP hostname, otherwise the MAC.
data_description.message_access_point: Wireless clients only. Name from the UniFi device list, otherwise its MAC.
data_description.message_ip: Current IP address of the client.
data_description.message_mac: Off by default. Omitted when the display name is the MAC anyway.

persistent.name: Persistent notification
persistent.description: Messages in the Home Assistant sidebar. Applies to the cleanup run only; newly detected devices never create a persistent notification.

data.persistent_when_empty: Also create when nothing was removed

data_description.persistent_notification: Report of the cleanup run with details per removed client.
data_description.persistent_when_empty: Off means the message only appears when something was actually removed. The previous one then stays and keeps showing the last real run and its time.

purge_now.name: Run purge now
purge_now.description: Runs the purge immediately instead of waiting for the daily run.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only determine what would be removed. Nothing is deleted.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Optional. Without it, all configured UniFi hosts run.
